issues.description: The problem specification and UML indicate a private helper method singFarmSongVerse should accept an Animal parameter (singFarmSongVerse(animal: Animal): void). The template defines singFarmSongVerse with no parameter (private void singFarmSongVerse(/*Animal animal*/)), which differs from the expected signature. The solution implements singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal). This mismatch in the template method signature can confuse students about the intended parameter and how to access the animal inside the verse method.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template's singFarmSongVerse method signature to accept an Animal parameter (private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal)) and update its body to use that parameter. This aligns the template with the UML/specification and matches the solution's implementation.

issues.description: The problem statement explicitly asks to initialize the Farm's internal ArrayList in a constructor with no arguments (a no-arg constructor). The solution repository instead provides only a constructor taking an int initialCapacity (public Farm(int initialCapacity)) and lacks the no-argument constructor. This discrepancy means the solution does not match the specified constructor requirement and may confuse students (and samples) that expect new Farm() to compile.
issues.suggestedFix: Provide a no-argument constructor in the solution (public Farm() { this.animals = new ArrayList<>(); }) to match the specification, or update the problem statement to accept a constructor with an initialCapacity parameter. Prefer adding the no-arg constructor (and optionally keep an overloaded constructor with initialCapacity) so examples using new Farm() compile as expected.

issues.description: Constructor API mismatch for the Farm class: the problem statement explicitly requires a no-argument constructor that initializes the internal ArrayList (initialize the ArrayList in a constructor with no arguments), but the solution repository provides only a Farm(int initialCapacity) constructor. This creates a semantic/API inconsistency that prevents students from mapping the required no-arg Farm() constructor in the problem/template to the solution implementation and may cause confusion or failing tests that expect a no-arg constructor.
issues.suggestedFix: Provide a no-argument constructor in the solution (and/or template) to match the problem statement: add public Farm() { this.animals = new ArrayList<>(); } — optionally keep the Farm(int initialCapacity) overload, but ensure a public no-arg Farm() exists so the API matches the exercise description.
